historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 revenue growth: Q1 FY27 actual +8%, consistent with revenue CAGRs tempered for the GLP-1 volume surge and management's 6-8% long-term US Pharma operating-profit target. Equity CAGR is unusable (book value negative since FY2021).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity is negative across FY2021-FY2026 (buybacks plus opioid accrual), so equity CAGR is undefined and book-value anchors do not apply. EPS 5-yr CAGR is undefined because FY2021 EPS was -28.26 (opioid charge); the 3-yr EPS CAGR (15.2%) is flattered by FY2023's $25.23 base. Revenue CAGR (11-13%) overstates underlying growth: GLP-1 pass-through volume and the Jan-2025 Core Ventures consolidation added low-margin dollars. Owner-FCF CAGR (6.9%/7.2%) runs ~0.6-0.8pp below reported FCF CAGR because SBC and interest income grew faster than cash flow.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2021 3,738; FY2023 4,332; FY2026 5,293. Reported FCF FY2021 3,901; FY2023 4,601; FY2026 5,719. All FCF years include ~$500M/yr of opioid settlement payments.

scenario_narratives.base: The oligopoly holds and the mix shift does the work. Revenue grows 8% in FY27 (Q1 actual +8%) and decelerates to ~3% as GLP-1 volume growth normalises and Medical-Surgical separates; EBITDA margin drifts from 1.72% to 1.92% over ten years as Oncology & Multispecialty (segment profit +53% in FY26), RxTS (11-12% long-term profit growth target) and biopharma services outgrow core distribution, consistent with management's 12-14% adjusted-EPS algorithm once ~3-4pp of buyback accretion is removed. Opioid payments run to schedule with no material private-claim additions. Terminal value binds at the 18x cap, not Gordon.
scenario_narratives.bull: GLP-1 remains a multi-year volume tailwind (quarterly GLP-1 distribution revenue ~$15B, +24% YoY), US Oncology Network keeps adding practices, and the biopharma-services platform (CMS GLP-1 Bridge, access/affordability programs) scales as a genuinely higher-margin business: revenue grows 10% in FY27 fading to 3.5%, EBITDA margin reaches 2.12%. The Wellverse IPO in H2 CY2027 prices the remaining 87% at or above the Apollo mark and the market re-rates the core as a specialty/oncology platform rather than a wholesaler; terminal cap 20x, g 3.0%. This case needs several things to go right at once, which is why its weight is below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: Drug-pricing reform and PBM/distributor fee scrutiny compress the distributor spread while GLP-1 price deflation and Medicare negotiation shrink dollar revenue: growth drops to 5% then 2%, EBITDA margin compresses to 1.50% (back to the FY22-FY25 1.4-1.5% band), and a large pharmacy-chain customer is lost or repriced. Private opioid plaintiffs win settlements beyond the $5.66B accrued, the Wellverse separation incurs stranded costs and management distraction, and the market stops paying a 23x P/E for a 1.5%-margin business: terminal cap 14x, g 2.0%. Working-capital capture halves as growth slows.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value McKesson as the cash-generating distributor it is, not as the EPS-compounder its buyback algorithm presents. The component build strips the three things that flatter reported numbers: SBC is expensed and the count held flat (buybacks are then value-neutral), interest income is excluded from the unlevered flows, and the two large non-shareholder claims on consolidated cash flow - the $5.66B opioid schedule and ~$6.3B of minority interests including Apollo's 13% of Wellverse - are deducted in the bridge rather than ignored. Margins are built per year from EBITDA, D&A, capex, tax and the payables-float working-capital release, with the mix-driven expansion capped at 1.92% in base. The terminal value is capped at 18x year-10 owner FCF because a 1.9%-margin distributor's perpetuity should not be worth more than the market pays today (~20x EV/FCF).
key_risks_to_valuation: Opioid: private-plaintiff claims beyond the national settlement could add to the $5.66B accrual; each additional $1B is ~$7/share after discounting
Drug-pricing reform / PBM and distributor fee transparency rules compressing the spread on branded and specialty drugs - a 10bp EBITDA-margin shock is ~6% of EBITDA

GLP-1 dependence: a large share of recent revenue growth is pass-through GLP-1 volume at distribution margins; price cuts or a Medicare negotiation outcome shrink dollar revenue and the working-capital release with it
Customer concentration with national pharmacy chains (CVS, Walmart) and the loss or repricing of any one contract
NCI valuation: the oncology-JV minority claim is capitalised at 11x FY26 earnings; at 7x-18x the deduction ranges $2.4-6.1B ($20-52/share)
Wellverse separation execution: stranded costs, IPO window risk, and the remaining 87% being valued below the Apollo mark
Negative equity and rising gross debt leave no cushion if a margin or litigation shock coincides with a credit-market closure

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 116.59m cover-page count at 2026-07-31 (Q1 FY27 10-Q, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus the 0.5m dilutive spread between Q1 FY27 diluted (119.2m) and basic (118.7m) weighted averages. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. Buybacks ($4.75B FY26, $2.53B in Q1 FY27 alone) are the mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, $247M). McKesson publishes no combined 'SBC incl. equity-award taxes' figure and tags no net-share-settlement withholding line, so the add-back is used alone; at 0.06% of revenue the omission is immaterial to value.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. CAPM: 10y UST ~4.2%, MCK 5-year beta ~0.55, ERP 5.0% gives cost of equity ~7.0%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.9% on $9.7B of debt against a ~$105B market cap gives a mechanical WACC of ~6.8-7.0%. House rate set at 7.5%: the regression beta of a defensive distributor understates the operating leverage of a 1.7% EBITDA margin (a 20bp margin move is 12% of EBITDA) and the drug-pricing/PBM regulatory exposure. The same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios so risk is charged once (in the scenario weights), not twice. Sensitivity grid runs 5.5-9.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost ($433M FY26) is an operating expense already inside reported EBITDA, so the lease charge is in the flows and operating lease liabilities ($2.09B) are NOT added to net debt. Finance leases ($189M liability, $36M/yr principal) are 0.15% of EV and are ignored. One treatment, stated.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated EBITDA includes 100% of the oncology/specialty JVs and the Medical-Surgical business, so NCI is deducted in the equity bridge (never in the flows). Two classes: (1) non-redeemable NCI (Core Ventures 30%, SCRI 49%, PRISM Vision etc.) earned $337M in FY26 (vs $186M FY25, the first full year of Core Ventures); capitalised at 11x = $3.7B, a multiple between the ~7x implied by the Jan-2025 Core Ventures purchase price and the model's own 18x terminal cap. (2) Redeemable NCI at carrying/redemption value $2,563M at 2026-06-30, up from $943M at 2026-03-31 on the June-2026 sale of a 13% Medical-Surgical (Wellverse) stake to Apollo for $1.25B. The Apollo cash is inside the June cash balance, so the matching claim must sit in the bridge. Q1 FY27 NCI income of $418M in a single quarter is treated as non-recurring (FY26 full-year was $337M) and is not capitalised.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1 (operating company); no prior valuation or MEMORY entry for MCK. McKesson is a thin-margin, high-volume pharmaceutical distributor (FY26 gross margin 3.6%, EBITDA margin 1.72%) with faster-growing oncology, biopharma-services and RxTS platforms carrying the profit growth. NEGATIVE shareholders' equity throughout the history (buybacks + opioid accrual) is a capital-structure feature, not a data error, so equity CAGR and book-value anchors are not used. Owner FCF = reported FCF 5,719 - SBC 247 - interest income 179 = 5,293: interest income is stripped although the company is net-debt because the component build is unlevered (EBITDA-based) and the cash earning it is netted inside net_debt; neither interest income nor interest expense belongs in the flows. DATA FLAGS for the parser: (a) CSV TotalDebt (11,026 at Jun-26, 7,793 at Mar-26) double-counts the current portion of long-term debt; us-gaap:LongTermDebt is 9,729 / 6,526 and LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations (noncurrent) 8,432 / 5,259 - the DB has summed the two. This valuation uses 9,729. (b) CSV CapEx FY2026 = 436 is PP&E only (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment) while FY2025 = 859 is PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets incl. $322M capitalised software; FY26 comparable total is 436 + 309 software = 745. The capex_pct path (0.19%) is built on the inclusive figure. (c) CSV NetIncome is consolidated incl. NCI (FY26 5,099 vs attributable ~4,762 = EPS 38.55 x 124.1m). Opioid: $5.66B accrued (LitigationReserveNoncurrent 5,058 at Jun-26 + ~$600M current portion) payable through ~FY2038 at ~$500-550M/yr; the payments are NOT in the component flows (the charge was taken FY2020-21), so the PV of the remaining schedule (~$4.2B at 7.5%, treated as gross with no tax shield) is deducted in the bridge. Private-plaintiff claims beyond the national settlement are an unquantified overhang carried in the bear weight. Wellverse separation (Med-Surg IPO targeted H2 CY2027): value-neutral in this model - the segment's 100% flows stay in consolidated EBITDA and Apollo's 13% is deducted via redeemable NCI; an IPO would convert the remaining 87% to cash/listed stock at whatever the market pays, which the narrative treats as a potential re-rating catalyst rather than a modelled value. Valuation date is six months into FY2027; FY2027 is discounted one full period (end-of-year convention, house standard), which is slightly conservative.

base.growth_rationale: Q1 FY27 revenue +8%; GLP-1 and oncology volume keep FY27 high-single-digit, then decelerate toward ~3% nominal (drug price inflation plus utilisation) as GLP-1 growth normalises and Wellverse (~3% of revenue) separates.
base.margin_rationale: FY26 EBITDA margin 1.72%. Management's 12-14% adjusted-EPS target with ~3-4pp from buybacks implies operating-profit growth of 8-10% on 6-8% revenue growth: 2-3bp/yr of mix-driven expansion as oncology/RxTS/biopharma services outgrow distribution. Capped at 1.92%.
base.tax_rationale: FY26 cash taxes paid 1,211 on ~5,965 EBIT = 20.3%, partly flattered by opioid-payment deductions; held at 22% (GAAP effective rate band 20-23%). No NOL or valuation-allowance effects.
base.wc_rationale: Distributor payables float: payables exceed receivables plus inventory, so revenue growth releases cash. FY26 capture ~1.4% of the revenue increase, FY25 ~4.5% (both after ~$500M opioid outflows); 2.0% is below the two-year average. Positive sign is deliberate and balance-sheet verified.
base.capex_rationale: PP&E 436 + capitalised software 309 = 745 in FY26 (0.185% of revenue); FY25 859 (0.24%). D&A 729 (0.18%) incl. $276M acquisition-intangible amortisation.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 20/55/25. Bear raised to 20%: the opioid private-claim tail is open-ended, shareholders' equity is -$3.9B with debt rising ($2.25B Term Loan B in Q1 FY27) so there is no balance-sheet cushion against a regulatory margin shock, and the stock is within 10% of its all-time high. Bull cut to 25%: it requires GLP-1 growth, oncology practice additions, RxTS margin scaling and a successful Wellverse IPO to all land together. Base carries the remainder because the three-player oligopoly and the FY27 guidance raise (adj. EPS $44.20-45.00, +13-15%) make the central path well-evidenced.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
